notes: django.urls.resolve(path) over 50 path() patterns, then the matched class-based view is called with a bare HttpRequest and picks the handler by method. No middleware, no response; a 405 answers None.
details: A Django URL pattern has no HTTP method, so the 100 routes are 50 patterns, each with a class-based view of two methods (get and post, or get and put). One call is django.urls.resolve(path), then the resolved view function with an HttpRequest made once per fixture: View.as_view creates the view object and View.dispatch chooses the handler by method. settings.configure(ROOT_URLCONF=...) is the only set-up; django.setup() is not needed and no middleware runs. http_method_not_allowed is overridden to return None, because the default builds a 405 response and logs a warning.
